2. Plaintiff's case was that the suit-land originally belonged to one Paklu Sheikh and his name was recorded in the last C.S. Khatian and the total area of the suit-land was 3.95 acres out of which Peklu Sheikh sold 1.01 acres to one Abdur Rahim and retained 2.94 acres in his possession; that Peklu Sheikh died leaving behind one wife Bachachu Mui, five sons, Kalo, Nalto, Jalo, Nalo and Ayenuddin and four daughters, Basiron, Nasiron, Mahiron and Kafiran, that on the death of the said Peklu Sheikh, his aforesaid heirs inherited the lands. Thereafter, Bachchu Mui died leaving behind only two sons, Kalu and Nalo and 4 daughters as named above; then Mohirun died leaving behind her husband Osman and 2 sons Rustom and Sekandar; that Rustom and Osman, out of their share of the suit-lands, sold 17½ acre of land to Jalo Sk. and his son by a registered deed dated 19.3.66 Meanwhile, Jalo Sheikh, out of his share for an area of .36½ acre of land, transferred .35 acre of the suit-land to his son Majibar and daughter Shahida Khatoon by a registered deed of Heba-bil-Ewaz dated 20.8.60; that the defendant No. 11 Shahida Khatoon sold and transferred .17½ acre of her land to the Plaintiff-petitioner by a registered deed of sale dated 22.5.74 and Defendant No. 9 Majibar sold .17½ acre of land to the Plaintiff by another registered deed of sale dated 25.3.74 and, thereafter, Sekandar Ali, defendant No. 33, son of Mohiran, also sold .08 acre of land to the Plaintiff by another registered deed of sale dated 7.6.80; thus the Plaintiff-petitioner in all acquired .43 acre of land and became a co-sharer in the suit jote; that the further case of the Plaintiff is that the Plaintiff reconeyed . 17½ acre of land to the vendor Mojibur and then Mojibur sold out the same to one Awaf and then again the said Awaf sold out the same to the Plaintiff; that the plaintiff has been in ejmali possession of the suit lands, but there has been inconvenience and trouble with respect to his ejmali possession. Hence, he requested the defendants to make an amicable partition of the suit lands, but they refused to do so. The Plaintiff therefore filed the present suit for partition. 

 8. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate for the contesting Opposite Parties, on the other hand, has submitted that the submission of the learned Advocate for the Petitioner on the 1st. point is not based on the evidence on record. The Judgments of the Courts below clearly show that on the question of the genuineness of the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed, both the Courts below, on proper consideration of the evidence on record, have come to a concurrent finding that the alleged Heba-bil-Ewaz deed is a fake and fraudulent one and the same has not been acted upon at any time. The finding on the question of genuineness of a document, namely, the Heba-bil-Ewaz, in the instant suit is, a finding of fact which has been arrived at by both the Courts concurrently, on proper and correct appreciation and consideration of the materials on record, having given elaborate reasoning and that being the position, this Court, in revision, cannot go into such a question of fact unless the Plaintiff- petitioner is able to show that such concurrent finding of fact is a perverse one or based on no evidence or on misreading of evidence. I have gone through the judgments of both the Courts below. The certified copy of the alleged Heba-bil-Ewaz deed has been produced by the Plaintiff which has been marked as Ext. 'X'. In order to prove the said deed, the Plaintiff himself as P.W.1 is the only witness. His other 2 witnesses have not said anything about the disputed Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed. Neither the scribe of the alleged Hiba-bil-Ewaz deed, nor any of the witnesses of the said deed has been examined by the Plaintiff and further, the alleged recipients of the Heba-bil-Ewaz deed, namely, Majibor Mia and Shahida Khatoon, though have been made parties in the instant suit and are alive, have not been examined by the Plaintiff, as witnesses to prove the genuineness of the disputed Heba-bil-Ewaz deed. Both the Courts below appear to have considered different aspects of the matter, namely, as to why the names of Majibor Mia and Shahida Khatoon, the alleged vendors of the Plaintiff, were not recorded in the R.S. Khatian, which was still appearing in the name of Jalo Sheikh, the original owner and again if the Plaintiff could really acquire title over the disputed .35 acre of the suit-land by purchase from Majibor and Shahida, how the same-land could be transferred by the same vendor to some other persons subsequently. It appears that the appellate Court further considered other aspects of the matter as to how one of the recipients of the alleged Heba-bil-Ewaz Majibor Mia being a minor at the time of the alleged Heba-bil- Ewaz could pay the consideration i.e. ewaz to the doner and what was the source of his income.
